consumed.resolution: Retired by operator decision 2026-11-03 (docs/plans/architecture-decisions-2026-11.md AD2-0): D3: each measured refusal was a correct drop. Replaced by arch-decisions-ad3-2 (a declared directory with a protected path beneath it routes to the console). Reopen at more than 15 percent empty commitments in a wave.

fix: Give each lane an ordered menu of in-scope alternates (triagecap.ExpandWithClusterMates already builds menus) so triage can re-select within scope; prefer this over a correction-loop re-dispatch of triage (the orchestrator files that path runs through are protected). Measure first: count refusals and no-work ends per wave after F29 lands.
notes: Architecture review of F29 (2026-09-26): re-selection is recovery, not admission; in-lane alternates fit better than reviewWithCorrections re-dispatch.
priority_rationale: inbox review 2026-09-27: Speculative until the census shows refusals exceed supply; the queue has no alternates to seed.
summary: A fleet lane's scope is ONE item, so when triage's breaker refuses its card (TRIAGE_PROTECTED_SURFACE) or the item turns out already done, the lane has nothing to fall back on and the cycle ends without shipping. F29 moves most doomed items to the console at seed time, but an undeclared item whose surface only the LLM derives can still reach a lane.
title: F32: a lane refused at triage has no alternative — seed lanes with in-scope alternates
